title: Inventory Tracker
spec: Write a function `inventory(records)` where the input is a list of lists. Each inner list contains a plain text product name, an initial quantity integer, a sold quantity integer, and a minimum threshold integer. Calculate the remaining quantity. If the remaining quantity falls below the threshold, calculate a reorder amount required to bring the stock up to exactly double the threshold. Return a list of lists containing the product name and the calculated reorder amount. Example input: [['apple', 50, 45, 10]]. The remaining is five, the threshold is ten, and the target is twenty, so the reorder amount is fifteen. Example output: [['apple', 15]].

title: Text Wrapper
spec: Write a function `wrap(text, limit)` that takes a single string of words separated by spaces and a maximum line length integer. Process the words sequentially to build lines of text, ensuring no line exceeds the maximum length. Add exactly one space between words on the same line. If a single word is strictly longer than the maximum length, place it on its own line and truncate it to the exact limit. Return a list of strings representing the wrapped lines. Example input: 'the quick brown fox', 8. Example output: ['the', 'quick', 'brown', 'fox'].

title: Water Trapping
spec: Write a function `rain(heights)` that accepts a list of non-negative integers representing the elevation of terrain on a two dimensional grid. Calculate how much water can be trapped between the peaks after a rainstorm. Determine the maximum height to the left and to the right of every position. The water level at any position is the minimum of these two maximum heights minus the terrain height at that position. Sum the trapped water amounts across all positions and return the total integer volume. Example input: [0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 1, 3]. Example output: 4.

title: Moving Average Smoothing
spec: Write a function `smooth(prices, window)` that takes a list of numbers and an integer window size. Calculate the simple moving average for each valid window of consecutive numbers in the list. For any position where a full window of the specified size cannot be formed, omit it from the result entirely. Return a list of the average values rounded to two decimal places. Example input: [1, 2, 3, 4] with window 2. Example output: [1.5, 2.5, 3.5].

title: Roman Numeral Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(numerals)` that accepts a list of two Roman numeral strings. Parse each string into its standard integer equivalent using basic addition and subtraction rules for Roman numerals. Add the two integer values together. Convert this integer sum back into a valid Roman numeral string. Return the resulting sum string. Example input: ['XIV', 'LX']. The values are fourteen and sixty, summing to seventy four. Example output: 'LXXIV'.

title: Run Length Compressor
spec: Write a function `compress(text)` that processes a single string of alphabetic characters. Count the lengths of consecutive identical characters. Compress sequences only if the same character appears three or more times in a row, replacing the sequence with the character itself followed by the integer count. Leave single and double characters completely unmodified. Return the newly compressed string. Example input: 'AABBBCCCCDAA'. Example output: 'AAB3C4DAA'.

title: Sentence Capitalizer
spec: Write a function `capitalize(text)` where the input is a single string containing multiple sentences separated by standard punctuation marks like periods, exclamation points, or question marks. Ensure the first alphabetic character of every sentence is capitalized. Also, normalize all whitespace by replacing any sequence of multiple spaces or tabs with a single space. Return the corrected string. Example input: 'hello world.  how are you? fine.' Example output: 'Hello world. How are you? Fine.'

title: IP Subnet Calculator
spec: Write a function `subnet(addresses)` where the input is a list of IPv4 address strings. Convert each address into a thirty two bit integer by splitting the octets and shifting them appropriately. Determine if all the provided addresses belong to the same exact subnet when applying a twenty four bit mask. Return a list containing a boolean indicating if they share the subnet, followed by the base network address string. Example input: ['192.168.1.5', '192.168.1.12']. Example output: [true, '192.168.1.0'].

title: Elevator Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(requests)` taking a list of destination floors requested in a building. The elevator starts at floor zero. It moves one floor at a time towards the currently targeted requested floor, taking one unit of time per floor traveled. It always pauses for exactly two units of time to open and close doors upon reaching the destination. Calculate the total units of time required to service all requests sequentially in the exact order provided. Return the total integer time. Example input: [3, 1]. Example output: 9.

title: Poker Hand Evaluator
spec: Write a function `rank(cards)` taking a list of five strings representing playing cards, using a format like '10H' for ten of hearts or 'AS' for ace of spades. Parse the suits and values to determine the poker hand achieved. Check for a flush if all suits match, and check for a straight if the values form a sequence. Return an integer representing the tier of the hand, where a straight flush is tier eight, a flush is tier five, a straight is tier four, and high card is tier zero. Example input: ['2H', '3H', '4H', '5H', '6H']. Example output: 8.

title: Vending Machine Change
spec: Write a function `change(amount)` where the input is an integer representing the amount of change to return in cents. You have an unlimited supply of standard quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies. Calculate the fewest number of coins needed to make the exact change. Return a list of four integers representing the required count of quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies respectively. Example input: 68. Example output: [2, 1, 1, 3].

title: Time Overlap Finder
spec: Write a function `schedule(meetings)` taking a list of lists, where each inner list contains two integers representing the start and end times of a meeting. Sort the meetings by their start times and merge any overlapping or touching intervals. Then, find the gaps between these merged meetings that represent free time blocks. Return a list of lists representing these free time intervals. Example input: [[1, 3], [2, 4], [6, 8]]. The merged intervals are one to four and six to eight. Example output: [[4, 6]].

title: Labyrinth Path Route
spec: Write a function `navigate(steps)` where the input is a list of strings, each containing an instruction like forward, left, or right, followed by a space and an integer distance. Starting at coordinates zero zero facing north, process each instruction sequentially to track your position on a grid. Left and right commands change your facing direction by ninety degrees, and the distance indicates how many units to move in the current direction. Calculate your final distance from the origin using the Manhattan distance formula and return this integer. Example input: ['forward 5', 'right 90', 'forward 3']. Example output: 8.

title: Pagination Generator
spec: Write a function `paginate(parameters)` where the input is a list containing three integers: the current page number, the total number of pages, and the number of siblings to show on each side of the current page. Generate a strictly increasing sequence of page numbers to display. Always include the first and last pages, and insert a negative one to represent gaps where intermediate page numbers are skipped. Return the list of integers. Example input: [4, 10, 1]. Example output: [1, -1, 3, 4, 5, -1, 10].

title: Anagram Groups
spec: Write a function `anagrams(words)` taking a list of lowercase string words. Group the words that have the exact same characters in any order. Sort each group of words alphabetically. Then, sort the overall list of groups by the size of the group in descending order, resolving ties by comparing the first word of each group alphabetically. Return the nested list of strings. Example input: ['tar', 'rat', 'art', 'bat']. Example output: [['art', 'rat', 'tar'], ['bat']].

title: Color Gradient Interpolator
spec: Write a function `gradient(colors, steps)` where the first input is a list containing two color lists, each with three integers for red, green, and blue values, and the second input is an integer for the number of intermediate steps. Calculate the linear interpolation for each color channel between the start and end colors, dividing the difference evenly across the steps. Return a list of lists containing the rounded integer color values for each step sequence, including the start and end colors. Example input: [[0, 0, 0], [10, 20, 30]], 1. Example output: [[0, 0, 0], [5, 10, 15], [10, 20, 30]].

title: Traffic Light Controller
spec: Write a function `traffic(events)` taking a list of integers representing arrival times in seconds of cars at a single lane one way traffic light. The light alternates between green for thirty seconds and red for thirty seconds, starting green at time zero. When the light is green, one car can pass every two seconds. When red, cars queue up and wait. Calculate the exact departure time for every car in the queue. Return a list of integers representing these departure times. Example input: [28, 29, 30]. Example output: [28, 30, 60].

title: Checksum Validator
spec: Write a function `checksum(message)` where the input is a string of alphabetic characters. Clean the string by converting it to uppercase and removing any non alphabetic characters. Convert each remaining character to its alphabetical index where A is one, B is two, and Z is twenty six. Multiply each alphabetical value by its position index in the cleaned string starting from one. Sum all these individual products together and take the remainder when the total sum is divided by eleven. Return the integer remainder. Example input: 'a b C!'. The cleaned string is 'ABC', and the sum is one times one plus two times two plus three times three, which is fourteen. Example output: 3.

title: Baseball Statistics
spec: Write a function `baseball(events)` taking a list of strings representing the outcome of each at bat for a player: single, double, triple, homerun, walk, or out. Calculate the batting average, which is total hits divided by at bats excluding walks. Then calculate the slugging percentage, which is total bases divided by at bats excluding walks. Return a list with the two values rounded to three decimal places. Example input: ['single', 'out', 'walk', 'homerun']. Example output: [0.667, 1.667].

title: DNA Strand Translator
spec: Write a function `translate(sequence)` where the input is a string of characters representing a DNA sequence. First, replace all occurrences of the letter T with the letter U to transcribe it to an RNA sequence. Then, divide the RNA sequence into sequential chunks of exactly three characters. Validate each chunk to ensure it contains only standard RNA letters. Count how many valid chunks match the sequence AUG, representing a start command, and how many match UAA, UAG, or UGA, representing a stop command. Return a list of two integers with these exact counts. Example input: 'ATGTAATAG'. Example output: [1, 2].

title: Log File Parser
spec: Write a function `filter(logs)` taking a list of string log entries. Each entry contains a four digit year in brackets, followed by a space, an uppercase severity level, a space, and a message. Extract the messages for all entries that have a severity of exactly ERROR or FATAL and occurred strictly between the years two thousand and two thousand and ten inclusive. Return a list of the extracted message strings. Example input: ['[2004] ERROR disk full', '[2012] ERROR timeout']. Example output: ['disk full'].

title: Shopping Cart Discounter
spec: Write a function `checkout(items)` where the input is a list of lists. Each inner list contains a string for the item name, an integer price in cents, and an integer quantity. Calculate the initial total cost of all items. Apply a progressive discount: deduct five percent from any portion of the amount that exceeds one thousand cents, and deduct an additional ten percent from any portion that exceeds five thousand cents. Return the final integer price rounded down after deducting all discounts. Example input: [['book', 1000, 3]]. Example output: 2900.

title: Memory Game Scorer
spec: Write a function `memory(moves)` taking a list of boolean values representing whether a player successfully found a matching pair in a turn of a memory card game. The player starts with a score of zero. A successful match adds ten points, plus a consecutive streak bonus of five points for each unbroken previous success. A failure resets the streak to zero and deducts exactly two points from the total score. Return the integer final score. Example input: [true, true, false, true]. Example output: 33.

title: Temperature Trend Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(temperatures)` where the input is a list of integers representing daily temperature readings. Identify the longest consecutive sequence of days where the temperature strictly increased each consecutive day. Calculate the total absolute temperature change from the very first day to the very last day of this longest warming streak. Return the integer difference. If there are no increases at all, return zero. Example input: [10, 12, 15, 11, 14]. Example output: 5.

title: Password Strength Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(passwords)` taking a list of candidate password strings. Check each string against a set of rules: it must be at least eight characters long, contain at least one uppercase letter, contain at least one lowercase letter, and contain at least one digit. Count how many passwords in the list meet all of these criteria simultaneously. Return the integer count of valid passwords. Example input: ['weak', 'Strong123', 'NoDigitsHere', 'another1']. Example output: 1.

title: Bowling Game Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(rolls)` that calculates the total points for a standard ten pin bowling game. The input is a list of integers representing the pins knocked down in each roll. The logic must process ten frames, where a strike awards ten points plus the next two rolls, a spare awards ten points plus the next roll, and an open frame awards the sum of its two rolls. Return the final integer score. Example: input [10, 7, 3, 9, 0, 10, 10, 10, 2, 8, 6, 4, 10, 10, 10] outputs 199.

title: Sudoku Grid Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(grid)` that determines if a nine by nine completely filled numerical board is valid. The input is a list of nine lists, each containing integers from one to nine. The logic must verify that every row contains all nine digits exactly once, every column contains all nine digits exactly once, and each of the nine three by three subgrids contains all nine digits exactly once. Return true if the board is valid and false otherwise. Example: a valid standard solution board returns true, but altering any single number to duplicate a value in its row returns false.

title: Algebraic Expression Multiplier
spec: Write a function `multiply(first, second)` that computes the product of two polynomials. Both inputs are lists of integers representing coefficients, ordered from the zero degree term up to the highest degree term. The logic must create a result list of zeros with a length equal to the sum of the two input lengths minus one. It must then iterate through every combination of terms, multiply the coefficients, and add the product to the result list at the index equal to the sum of the two original indices. Return the final list of combined integer coefficients. Example: multiplying [1, 2] and [3, 4] produces [3, 10, 8].

title: Cache Eviction Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(requests, capacity)` that tracks items in a least recently used cache. The first parameter is a list of integer identifiers accessed over time, and the second is the maximum number of items the cache can hold. When a new identifier is accessed and the cache is full, the item that has not been accessed for the longest time must be removed. Return a list of identifiers representing the evicted items in the exact order they were removed. Example: processing requests [1, 2, 3, 1, 4] with capacity 2 outputs [2, 3].

title: Daily Stock Spans
spec: Write a function `spans(prices)` that calculates the consecutive number of days up to the current day where the asset price was less than or equal to today. The input is a list of daily integer prices. The logic must use a decreasing stack structure to efficiently find the previous day that had a strictly greater price, computing the span as the difference in days. Return a list of integer spans corresponding to each day. Example: given input prices [100, 80, 60, 70, 60, 75, 85] the output is [1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 4, 6].

title: Codebreaker Game Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(secret, guess)` that compares a hidden sequence of four digits against an attempted sequence. Both inputs are lists of four integers. The logic must count the exact matches where the digit and position are correct, and the partial matches where a correct digit is in the wrong position. A digit in the hidden sequence can only be matched once per evaluation. Return a list containing two integers: the exact match count and the partial match count. Example: with secret [1, 8, 0, 7] and guess [7, 8, 1, 0] the output is [1, 3].

title: Weight Bin Packer
spec: Write a function `pack(weights, capacity)` that distributes a list of item weights into the minimum number of containers of a fixed maximum size. The logic must first sort the items from heaviest to lightest. Then, it must place each item into the first available container that has enough remaining space, creating a new container only if it does not fit into any existing one. Return a list of lists, where each inner list represents the weights placed in a single container. Example: inputs [4, 8, 1, 4, 2, 1] and capacity 10 outputs [[8, 2], [4, 4, 1, 1]].

title: Four In A Row Checker
spec: Write a function `check(grid)` that finds whether a player has won on a standard seven by six gravity board. The input is a list of lists where empty slots are zero, player one is one, and player two is two. The logic must scan all horizontal, vertical, and both diagonal directions to detect if four consecutive matching nonzero pieces exist anywhere on the board. Return the integer of the winning player, or zero if no one has won. Example: a column containing [0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2] from top to bottom returns 1.

title: Profit Maximizer Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(jobs)` that selects a non overlapping set of tasks to yield the highest total profit. The input is a list of lists, where each inner list contains three integers: start time, end time, and monetary reward. The logic must sort the jobs by their end times and use dynamic programming to compute the maximum possible reward up to each job, deciding whether to include or exclude it by finding the most recent compatible predecessor. Return the maximum total integer profit. Example: jobs [[1, 2, 50], [3, 5, 20], [6, 19, 100], [2, 100, 200]] yields 250.

title: Minefield Blank Reveal
spec: Write a function `reveal(board, click)` that updates a grid when a player targets an empty cell. The board is a list of lists containing integers where negative one represents a hidden mine and zero through eight are adjacent mine counts. The click is a list of two integers representing the row and column chosen. If the clicked cell is a zero, the logic must recursively or iteratively reveal all neighboring cells in all eight directions, continuing outward as long as it hits other zeros. Return the updated board where revealed non mine cells remain their original numbers and untouched cells are masked as negative two. Example: a click on a corner zero reveals an entire connected section of safe spaces.

title: Closest Word Matcher
spec: Write a function `suggest(word, dictionary)` that finds the most similar text string from a provided list of valid terms. The logic must calculate the edit distance between the target string and every term in the list, counting the minimum number of character insertions, deletions, and substitutions required to transform one into the other. Return the valid term that has the smallest edit distance to the target, breaking ties by choosing the term that appears first in the dictionary list. Example: inputs kitten and [sitting, mitten, fitting] outputs mitten.

title: Task Dependency Resolver
spec: Write a function `resolve(tasks)` that orders a series of operations so that all prerequisite conditions are met before an operation begins. The input is a list of lists, where each inner list contains a task integer identifier followed by zero or more prerequisite task identifiers. The logic must build an adjacency structure and compute in degrees for each task, then process a queue of tasks with no pending prerequisites to build the execution sequence. Return a single list of ordered task identifiers, or an empty list if a circular dependency exists. Example: input [[1, 2], [2, 3], [3]] outputs [3, 2, 1].

title: Image Kernel Filter
spec: Write a function `apply(image, kernel)` that performs a two dimensional convolution operation on a grayscale image. Both inputs are lists of lists of integers, where the kernel is always a three by three grid. The logic must iterate over every pixel of the original image, center the kernel on it, multiply the overlapping values, and sum them to produce the new pixel value, assuming zero padding for edges. Return the newly generated list of lists of integers. Example: applying a kernel of all ones to an image of a single centered pixel with value ten outputs a three by three block of tens.

title: Image Contrast Enhancer
spec: Write a function `enhance(pixels)` that adjusts the intensities of a grayscale image to evenly distribute the contrast. The input is a flat list of integers ranging from zero to two hundred fifty five. The logic must count the occurrences of each brightness level, compute the cumulative distribution, and map each original value to a new value scaled proportionally to the maximum possible brightness. Return a new flat list of transformed integer intensities. Example: an input heavily clustered around fifty will output a list where values are spread smoothly across the entire zero to two fifty five range.

title: Cellular Automaton Generation
spec: Write a function `evolve(grid, steps)` that computes the future state of a biological simulation. The grid is a list of lists containing zeros for dead cells and ones for live cells. For each generation step, the logic must evaluate every cell simultaneously: a live cell with two or three live neighbors survives, a dead cell with exactly three live neighbors becomes alive, and all other cells die or remain dead. Return the final list of lists after the specified number of steps. Example: a three by one horizontal line of live cells oscillates into a one by three vertical line after one step.

title: Rolling Hash Searcher
spec: Write a function `search(text, pattern)` that finds all starting indices of a target sequence within a larger document. The logic must convert characters to integer values and compute a hash for the pattern and the initial text window using a prime modulus. It must then slide the window one character at a time, updating the hash by subtracting the leading character and adding the trailing character, only performing a full string comparison if the hashes match. Return a list of integer indices where the pattern occurs. Example: searching for aaba in aabaacaaba outputs [0, 6].

title: Branching Tree Plotter
spec: Write a function `generate(iterations)` that calculates the two dimensional line segments of a fractal canopy. The logic starts with a single vertical trunk originating at coordinate zero zero. For each iteration, every existing endpoint spawns two new branches at fixed symmetric outward angles, with the new segment length reduced by a fixed scaling factor from its parent. Return a list of lists, where each inner list contains four floating point numbers representing the start horizontal, start vertical, end horizontal, and end vertical coordinates of a segment. Example: zero iterations returns just the trunk segment.

title: Quadtree Image Compressor
spec: Write a function `compress(image)` that converts a square two dimensional grid into a recursive region structure. The input is a list of lists containing integer pixel values, where the dimensions are a power of two. The logic must recursively divide the grid into four equal quadrants. If a quadrant contains only identical pixel values, it is represented as a single list containing that integer. If it contains mixed values, it must be represented as a list containing the four sub quadrants in top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right order. Return the fully compressed hierarchical list structure. Example: a two by two grid of all ones returns just [1].

title: Triangular Arbitrage Detector
spec: Write a function `detect(rates)` that looks for risk free profit opportunities across three currency conversions. The input is a list of lists representing a complete conversion matrix between several currencies, where the value at row x and column y is the exchange rate. The logic must iterate through all combinations of three distinct currencies and multiply the rates from the first to the second, the second to the third, and the third back to the first. Return a list of three integer currency indices if a product greater than one is found, otherwise return an empty list. Example: rates creating a cycle product of one point zero five will return the three indices involved.

title: Artist Spaced Shuffler
spec: Write a function `shuffle(tracks)` that randomly reorders a music playlist while ensuring no two consecutive songs belong to the same creator. The input is a list of lists, where each inner list contains a song title and an artist name. The logic must count the frequencies of each artist, prioritize placing songs by the most frequent remaining artists, and randomly select among valid candidates to build the output sequence. Return the reordered list of tracks, or an empty list if a valid sequence is impossible due to one artist dominating the list. Example: inputs of two songs by artist A and one by artist B must output an A, B, A sequence.

title: Bounded Stops Router
spec: Write a function `route(flights, source, destination, limit)` that finds the cheapest airfare between two cities under a maximum number of connections. The flights input is a list of lists containing origin integer, destination integer, and integer price. The logic must use a breadth first search or modified shortest path algorithm that tracks both the accumulated cost and the number of stops, exploring outward level by level up to the specified limit and avoiding more expensive paths that take the same or more stops. Return the lowest integer price found, or negative one if no route exists. Example: a direct flight costing hundred is chosen over a fifty cost flight that exceeds the allowed stops.

title: Sequence Difference Finder
spec: Write a function `compare(original, revised)` that computes the additions and removals needed to change one document into another. Both inputs are lists of words. The logic must use dynamic programming to build a grid of lengths for the longest common subsequence between the prefixes of the two lists. Once the grid is complete, trace backward from the end to classify each word as kept, added, or removed. Return a list of lists where each element pairs a word with an action string indicator. Example: comparing [apple, banana] to [apple, orange] outputs pairing apple with kept, banana with removed, and orange with added.

title: Center Expand Palindrome
spec: Write a function `expand(text)` that finds the longest symmetrical sequence of characters within a string. The input is a single string of lowercase letters. The logic must loop through every character and every space between characters, treating each as a potential center of a palindrome, and expand outward in both directions as long as the left and right characters match. It must track the starting index and length of the largest valid expansion found. Return the longest palindromic substring. Example: input racecar outputs racecar, while input abababaa outputs abababa.

title: Team Division Checker
spec: Write a function `divide(members)` that determines if a group can be split into two opposing factions without any internal conflicts. The input is a list of lists, where the index represents a person and the inner list contains the integers of people they refuse to be grouped with. The logic must use a graph coloring algorithm, assigning each unvisited person to one team and placing all their conflicts into the opposite team via breadth first or depth first traversal. Return true if a valid division is possible, and false if any person is forced into both teams simultaneously. Example: an input of [[1], [0, 2], [1]] returns true because person zero and two can be on team A while person one is on team B.

title: Telephone Keypad Combinations
spec: Write a function `combinations(digits)` that translates a sequence of numeric pushes into all possible text messages. The input is a string of numbers from two to nine. The logic must map each digit to its corresponding traditional mobile phone letters, such as mapping two to a, b, and c. It must use backtracking or an iterative queue to build sequences, appending each possible letter for the current digit to all prefixes generated by the previous digits. Return a list of all valid resulting strings in any order. Example: the input two three outputs nine strings including ad, ae, af, bd, and so on.

title: Recipe Scaler
spec: Write a function `scale(recipe, factor)` to adjust ingredient quantities. The recipe is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains an ingredient name, a numeric quantity, and a unit string. Multiply the quantity by the scaling factor. If the new quantity is three or more teaspoons, convert the unit to tablespoons and divide the quantity by three. If it is four or more tablespoons, convert to cups and divide by four. Calculate the sum of all original quantities and the sum of all scaled quantities. Return a new array where the first two elements are the original sum and the scaled sum, followed by formatted strings that join the scaled quantity, unit, and name with spaces.

title: Tax Bracket Assessor
spec: Write a function `assess(incomes)` that takes an array of integer incomes. For each income, calculate a progressive federal tax. The first ten thousand is untaxed. The amount from ten thousand to forty thousand is taxed at ten percent. The amount from forty thousand to one hundred thousand is taxed at twenty percent. Anything over one hundred thousand is taxed at thirty percent. Also calculate a flat two percent local tax on the entire income. Return an array of arrays, where each inner array contains the original income, the federal tax, the local tax, and the net remaining income.

title: Flight Route Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(flights)` that takes an array of flight segments. Each segment is an array containing an origin city, a destination city, a departure time in minutes from midnight, and a flight duration in minutes. Calculate the total travel time from the first departure to the final arrival. Calculate the total time spent flying. Calculate the total time spent in layovers between consecutive flights. Find the duration of the longest single layover. Return an array containing total travel time, total flight time, total layover time, and the maximum layover.

title: Dart Match Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(throws)` that processes an array of arrays representing darts thrown in a game of five hundred and one. Each inner array represents a turn of three throws, where each throw is a number from zero to sixty. A player starts at a score of five hundred and one. Subtract the sum of the turn from their total. If a turn would reduce their total below zero, to exactly one, or to zero without the last throw being an even number, the turn is a bust and their total resets to what it was at the start of the turn. Return the final score after all turns have been processed.

title: Rotor Cipher Simulator
spec: Write a function `encode(text)` that simulates a substitution cipher with a rotating alphabet. The initial alphabet is the standard twenty-six lowercase letters. For each letter in the input string, find its index in the current alphabet, replace it with the letter at that index in a reversed standard alphabet, and then shift the current alphabet by moving the first letter to the end. Spaces and punctuation are left unchanged and do not rotate the alphabet. Return the encoded string.

title: Code Minifier
spec: Write a function `minify(text)` that removes whitespace and comments from a string. It must iterate through the text character by character. If it encounters a double quote, it toggles a string state flag and preserves everything exactly as is until the next unescaped double quote. If it sees two forward slashes outside a string, it skips characters until a newline. Any spaces, tabs, or newlines outside of strings and comments are ignored entirely. All other characters are added to a result string. Return the compacted result string.

title: Billiards Collision
spec: Write a function `simulate(balls)` that takes an array of two balls, where each is an array of x position, y position, x velocity, y velocity, and radius. Calculate the relative position and relative velocity of the second ball with respect to the first. Find the quadratic equation coefficients for the distance between them over time. Calculate the discriminant to determine if their paths intersect. If the discriminant is negative or the calculated time of collision is negative, return negative one. Otherwise, return the time of collision rounded to three decimal places.

title: Markdown Table Builder
spec: Write a function `format(rows)` that takes an array of rows, where each row is an array of strings. Determine the maximum string length for each column across all rows. Create a separator string of dashes for each column matching its maximum length. Build an array of formatted strings where each cell is padded with trailing spaces to match the column width, and cells are joined by a vertical pipe character with one space on each side. Insert the separator row between the first and second rows. Return a single string joined by newlines.

title: Shipping Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(cart)` that takes an array of items, where each item is an array containing weight in kilograms, length, width, height in centimeters, and quantity. Calculate the total weight and the total volume of all items. The base shipping rate is ten dollars. Add an extra two dollars for every kilogram over five kilograms. Calculate the volume of each item to find the total cubic centimeters. Add a five dollar surcharge if the total volume exceeds ten thousand cubic centimeters. If there are more than ten items total, apply a fifteen percent discount to the final cost. Return the final shipping cost.

title: Polygon Metrics
spec: Write a function `metrics(vertices)` that takes an array of coordinate arrays, each containing an x and a y value, representing a closed polygon. Calculate the area using the shoelace formula by summing the cross products of each vertex and the next one, then halving the absolute total. Calculate the perimeter by summing the Euclidean distances between consecutive vertices, including the distance from the last vertex back to the first. Return an array containing the area and the perimeter, both rounded to two decimal places.

title: Receipt Printer
spec: Write a function `print(items)` that takes an array of items, where each item is an array containing a name string, a price number, and a boolean indicating if it is taxable. Calculate the subtotal of all items. Calculate a tax of eight percent only on the taxable items. Find the grand total. Format each item as a string padded to thirty characters, with the name on the left and the price on the right, filled with dots in the middle. Append three lines at the bottom for subtotal, tax, and total. Return the array of printed lines.

title: Kanban Simulator
spec: Write a function `process(actions)` that maintains three lists of tasks: backlog, active, and completed. The backlog initially contains integers one through five. It takes an array of actions, where each action is an array with a task identifier and a target list string. For each action, find the task in its current list, remove it, and append it to the target list. If the task is not found in any list, increment an error counter. After processing all actions, return an array containing the length of the backlog, the length of the active list, the length of the completed list, and the error count.

title: CPU Decoder
spec: Write a function `decode(instructions)` that takes an array of integers representing sixteen-bit machine code instructions. For each integer, extract the top four bits as the operation code, the next four bits as the register number, and the bottom eight bits as the immediate value. Map the operation code zero to load, one to add, two to store, and three to branch. Format a string for each instruction, for example describing it as load register five with forty-two. Return an array of these formatted assembly strings.

title: Heatmap Renderer
spec: Write a function `render(points)` that takes an array of data points, where each point is an array containing an x coordinate, a y coordinate, and an intensity value. The coordinates range from zero to nine. Create a ten by ten grid of zeroes. Add the intensity of each point to the corresponding grid cell. Find the maximum value in the grid. Convert each cell to a character based on its value relative to the maximum: a space for zero, a dot for less than a third, a dash for less than two thirds, and a hash for anything higher. Return an array of ten strings.

title: Chord Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(frets)` that takes an array of six integers representing the frets played on a guitar, with negative one for an unplayed string. Find the lowest and highest frets played, excluding zero and negative one. Calculate the fret stretch, which is the difference between the highest and lowest fret. Count how many unique non-zero frets are played to estimate the number of fingers required. A chord is considered playable if the stretch is less than or equal to four and the finger count is less than or equal to four. Return an array with the stretch, finger count, and a boolean for playability.

title: Swim Meet Scorer
spec: Write a function `tally(results)` that takes an array of race results, where each result is an array of team names in finishing order. The first place gets six points, second gets four, third gets three, fourth gets two, and fifth gets one. Accumulate the total points for each team across all races. Iterate through the totals to find the team with the highest score. Return an array containing the winning team name and their total points. If there are no results, return an empty string and zero.

title: Typing Speed Analyzer
spec: Write a function `evaluate(words)` that takes an array of typed words, where each element is an array containing the target word, the typed word, and the time in seconds taken to type it. Count the total characters in the target words. Count the number of incorrectly typed words. Sum the total time taken. Calculate the gross words per minute by dividing the total characters by five, then dividing by the total time in minutes. Calculate the net words per minute by subtracting the errors per minute from the gross words per minute. Return an array with gross words per minute, net words per minute, and accuracy percentage.

title: Envelope Generator
spec: Write a function `synthesize(notes)` that takes an array of notes, where each note is an array containing frequency, peak amplitude, and duration in milliseconds. For each note, calculate a basic attack, decay, sustain, and release envelope. The attack phase takes ten percent of the duration to reach peak amplitude. The decay takes twenty percent of the duration to drop to half the peak amplitude for the sustain. The release takes the last twenty percent of the duration to drop from half amplitude to zero. Return an array of arrays, where each inner array contains the four key time durations and the sustain amplitude.

title: Moon Phase Estimator
spec: Write a function `phase(days)` that takes an integer representing days since a known new moon. Calculate the exact cycles elapsed using the lunar month of twenty-nine point five three days. Find the remainder to determine the days into the current cycle. Calculate the illumination percentage using a sine wave approximation based on the fraction of the cycle completed. Determine the integer days remaining until the next full moon, which occurs halfway through the cycle. Return an array containing the cycle fraction, illumination percentage, and days to next full moon.

title: Word Search Solver
spec: Write a function `find(grid, word)` that takes a grid of letters as an array of strings, and a target word. Search every row and column for the first letter of the target word. When found, check all eight directions horizontally, vertically, and diagonally to see if the rest of the word matches. The search must handle grid boundaries properly so it does not check outside the grid. If the word is found, return an array containing the starting row, the starting column, the horizontal direction step, and the vertical direction step. If not found, return an array of four negative ones.

title: Morse Length Calculator
spec: Write a function `measure(message)` that takes a string of dots, dashes, and spaces. Calculate the time units required to transmit the message. A dot takes one unit, and a dash takes three units. The gap between symbols in the same letter takes one unit. A single space character in the string represents a gap between letters and takes three units. Two consecutive spaces represent a word gap and take seven units. Count the total dots, total dashes, and total units. Return an array of these three numbers.

title: Hex Grid Distance
spec: Write a function `distance(coords)` that takes an array of coordinate arrays, where each inner array contains axial q and r coordinates for a hexagonal grid. Convert each coordinate to cube coordinates x, y, and z, where x equals q, z equals r, and y equals negative q minus r. For each consecutive pair of coordinates, calculate the distance as the maximum of the absolute differences in their x, y, and z values. Accumulate these distances to find the total path length. Return the total length.

title: Text Justifier
spec: Write a function `justify(words, width)` that takes an array of word strings and a line width. Group words into lines such that adding another word and a space would exceed the width. For each full line, calculate the number of spaces needed to reach the exact width. Divide the spaces as evenly as possible between the words, with any extra spaces added to the leftmost gaps first. The last line should just be single-spaced and padded on the right with spaces. Return an array of the formatted line strings.

title: Reversi Move Flipper
spec: Write a function `flip(board, move)` that takes an eight by eight board represented as an array of strings with spaces, black pieces, and white pieces, and a move array containing row, column, and player color. Check all eight directions from the move. For each direction, step outward as long as the cell contains the opponent's color. If a cell with the player's color is then found, all opponent pieces in between are flanked. Create a new board with the piece placed and all flanked pieces flipped to the player's color. Return the updated board array.

title: Irrigation Planner
spec: Write a function `plan(plants)` that takes an array of plants, where each plant is an array of x coordinate, y coordinate, and water requirement in liters. Assume a sprinkler is at the origin zero, zero. First, find the distance of every plant from the origin. Find the maximum distance to determine the required sprinkler radius. Sum the total water required for all plants. Calculate the area covered by the sprinkler using pi times the radius squared. Return an array with the radius, total water, and covered area, all rounded to the nearest whole numbers.

title: Tennis Match Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(points)` that takes a string of characters where each character is either a one or a two, representing which player won the point. The function must track the game score using standard tennis rules: zero, fifteen, thirty, forty, and advantage. It must resolve games and track the number of games won by each player in a single set. The first player to reach six games with a margin of two wins the set. If the game score reaches six all, a tiebreak is played where the first to seven points with a margin of two wins. Return a list containing the final game count for player one followed by player two. For example, if player one wins twenty four consecutive points, the output is [6, 0].

title: Cryptocurrency Portfolio Rebalancer
spec: Write a function `rebalance(portfolio)` that accepts a list of lists where each inner list contains a digital asset ticker symbol, current amount held, current price per unit, and a target portfolio percentage as a decimal. The function must calculate the total value of all assets, determine the target monetary value for each asset based on its target percentage, and compute the difference from its current value. Finally, it should translate these value differences back into asset quantities to buy or sell. Return a list of lists showing the ticker symbol and the required quantity change, positive for buy and negative for sell. For example, an input like [["bitcoin", 1, 50000, 0.6], ["ethereum", 10, 3000, 0.4]] returns [["bitcoin", -0.044], ["ethereum", 0.733]] assuming rounding to three decimals.

title: Meeting Room Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(meetings)` that takes a list of pairs where each pair contains a start time and an end time represented as integer minutes from midnight. The function must assign each meeting to a room such that the minimum possible number of rooms is used. Two meetings can share a room if the end time of the first is less than or equal to the start time of the second. Track the busy periods for each room and allocate early meetings to available rooms first. Return the integer number of rooms required. For example, given [[540, 600], [570, 630], [600, 660]], the function returns 2.

title: Domino Chain Builder
spec: Write a function `chain(tiles)` that accepts a list of pairs representing dominoes, where each pair contains two integers denoting the dots on each half. The logic must find the length of the longest valid chain that can be formed by matching ends. Dominoes can be flipped so that the left and right numbers are swapped, but each domino can only be used once per chain. The function must explore all possible connections and track the maximum sequence length found. Return this maximum integer length. For example, given [[1, 2], [3, 4], [2, 3], [5, 6]], the output is 3 because the sequence from one to four uses three tiles.

title: Subway Fare Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(taps)` that takes a list of lists representing a sequence of transit tap events, where each event has an integer timestamp in minutes, a station identifier string, and an integer fare zone. Consecutive pairs of taps represent a single journey. For each journey, a base fare of three dollars is charged, plus one dollar for each zone boundary crossed. Additionally, there is a daily cap of twelve dollars; once a user accumulates twelve dollars in a single day, all subsequent trips on that same day are free. Assume a day ends at minute 1440. Track the running cost and daily accumulated fare. Return the total fare charged across all days as an integer. For example, given [[480, "alpha", 1], [510, "beta", 2], [600, "beta", 2], [630, "gamma", 4]], the output is 9.

title: Tournament Bracket Generator
spec: Write a function `bracket(players)` that accepts a list of strings representing player names. The function must determine the next highest power of two above or equal to the number of players, and add placeholder strings called bye to the list to reach that number. Then, it should divide the players into two halves, taking one from the front and one from the back sequentially to create match pairs for the first round. Keep track of the matchups and ensure no two byes are paired together. Return a list of pairs of strings. For example, given ["alice", "bob", "charlie"], the output should be [["alice", "bye"], ["bob", "charlie"]].

title: Library Late Fee Assessor
spec: Write a function `assess(records)` that takes a list of lists representing borrowed library items. Each inner list contains an integer checkout day, an integer return day, and an integer base value of the item. A loan is allowed for fourteen days. For every day late, a fee of two dollars is added, but the fee does not increase on days that are multiples of seven or days that follow multiples of seven, which act as weekends. Track the passing days and the accumulating fee. The maximum fee cannot exceed the base value of the item. Return a list of fees corresponding to each item. For example, given [[1, 20, 15], [5, 10, 30]], the output is [8, 0].

title: Restaurant Bill Splitter
spec: Write a function `split(diners)` that takes a list of lists where each element describes a person. Each diner record contains their name, a list of individual dish prices they ordered, and a list of shared appetizer prices they participated in. The cost of shared appetizers is divided equally among everyone at the table, regardless of who partook. The function must sum each person's individual items, add their portion of the shared total, apply an eight percent tax, and finally add a twenty percent tip on the post-tax amount. Return a list of total amounts owed by each person in the same order, rounded to two decimal places. For example, if two diners share a 10 dollar dish and one ordered a 5 dollar dish, that person owes 12.96.

title: Textile Pattern Generator
spec: Write a function `weave(dimensions)` that takes a list containing three integers: width, height, and border thickness. The logic must construct a two-dimensional grid representing a rug pattern using specific characters. The outer edge based on the border thickness must be filled with hash symbols. The inner area must be filled with dot symbols, except for a diagonal cross connecting the four inner corners made of plus symbols. Build the grid row by row, carefully tracking row and column indices to determine whether the current position is a border, a diagonal line, or background. Return a list of strings where each string is a row of the pattern. For example, given [5, 5, 1], the center row string would be a hash, dot, plus, dot, and hash.

title: Markdown List Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(text)` that accepts a single string containing multiple lines of text, separated by newline characters. Each line represents an item in an unordered list, prefixed by an asterisk and zero or more spaces. Two spaces of indentation represent one level of nesting. The function must read the lines sequentially, count the leading spaces to determine the nesting depth, and build a hierarchical structure composed of nested lists of strings. Maintain a stack of active lists and track the current indentation level. Return a deeply nested list reflecting the structure. For example, a parent item with a single nested child item will output as [["parent item", ["child item"]]].

title: Plumbing System Flow
spec: Write a function `flow(pipes)` that receives a list of lists, where each inner list contains a string source node, a string destination node, and an integer maximum capacity. The system starts at a node named origin and ends at a node named drain. The logic must simulate water flowing through the network by tracking the incoming water to each node and distributing it to outgoing pipes based on their individual capacities and the total water available. Nodes cannot output more water than they receive, nor can a pipe exceed its capacity. Return the maximum integer amount of water that can reach the drain. For example, given [["origin", "a", 10], ["a", "drain", 5]], the output is 5.

title: Ski Resort Lift Router
spec: Write a function `route(trails)` that accepts a list of trail connections, where each connection is a list containing a starting point string, an ending point string, and an integer difficulty rating from one to ten. The logic must find a path from the point named peak to the point named base that minimizes the maximum difficulty rating encountered on any single trail along the way, preferring shorter total path lengths as a tiebreaker. Explore the network, keep track of the easiest bottlenecks and distances, and return a list of strings representing the sequence of points on the best path. For example, given [["peak", "mid", 3], ["mid", "base", 4]], the output is ["peak", "mid", "base"].

title: Solar Panel Placement
spec: Write a function `place(roof)` that takes a list of lists of integers representing a grid of roof tiles, where each integer is the average daily sunlight in hours. The function must find a rectangular area of dimensions two tiles high by three tiles wide that maximizes the total sum of sunlight hours. Iterate through all possible starting positions that can fit the rectangle, sum the internal values using nested loops, and track the highest total found. Return a list containing two integers representing the row and column index of the top left corner of the best placement. For example, if the highest density area starts at the second row and third column, return [1, 2].

title: Drone Flight Path Optimizer
spec: Write a function `optimize(waypoints)` that accepts a list of lists, where each inner list contains integer coordinates for a location. The drone starts at the first location and must visit all other locations in the order provided before returning to the start. The function must calculate the total flight energy, which is the sum of straight line distances between consecutive points plus an additional turn penalty. The turn penalty adds five energy units for every direction change greater than forty five degrees between consecutive flight segments. Track the previous movement vectors and accumulate the total energy. Return the total integer energy cost. For example, a square path of side length ten might return 60, accounting for distances and turns.

title: Hotel Room Upgrade
spec: Write a function `upgrade(data)` that takes a list containing two sublists: a list of bookings and a list of available rooms. Each booking is a list containing a guest name, an integer loyalty tier from one to five, and a requested integer room class from one to three. Each available room is a list with a room number and its class. The logic must assign rooms to guests by first sorting guests by their loyalty tier descending. It should try to assign the requested class first; if unavailable, assign the next highest available class. Track room availability and update counts as assignments are made. Return a list of pairs matching guest names to their assigned room numbers. For example, given guest ["john", 5, 1] and available room [101, 2], the output could be [["john", 101]].

title: Railway Signal Network
spec: Write a function `signal(tracks)` that takes a list of strings representing the current state of a series of railway track blocks, where a train presence is denoted by an uppercase T and an empty block by a dash. Each block has an associated signal. The logic must determine the color of the signal for every block based on the positions of trains ahead. A signal is red if the immediate block contains a train, yellow if the immediate block is empty but the following block contains a train, and green otherwise. Track the indices of trains and evaluate the next blocks sequentially. Return a list of strings with the signal colors for each block in order. For example, given ["T", "-", "T", "-"], the output is ["red", "yellow", "red", "green"].

title: Escape Room Lock Simulator
spec: Write a function `unlock(actions)` that accepts a list of integers representing turn instructions for a three ring dial lock. The lock starts with all rings set to zero. Positive integers mean rotating the current active ring to the right by that many positions, while negative integers mean rotating to the left. A zero instruction means switching the active ring to the next inner ring. Each ring has ten positions numbered zero to nine, and rotating past nine wraps back to zero. Keep track of the current positions for all three rings and the currently active ring index. Return a list of three integers representing the final positions of the rings. For example, an input of [12, 0, -3] results in [2, 7, 0].

title: Warehouse Pallet Stacker
spec: Write a function `stack(boxes)` that takes a list of integer weights representing arriving boxes. Pallets can safely hold a maximum of one hundred weight units. The logic must place each box onto the current pallet until adding the next box would exceed the limit, at which point the current pallet is finalized and a new one is started. A box weighing more than the limit must be placed on its own pallet, discarding the limit constraint for that single item. Maintain a running sum for the current pallet and a master list of all packed pallets. Return a list of lists, where each inner list contains the weights of boxes on that pallet. For example, given [30, 40, 50, 110], the output is [[30, 40], [50], [110]].

title: Wind Farm Power Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate(speeds)` that accepts a list of integers representing the unhindered wind speed arriving at a line of turbines. The first turbine receives the full wind speed. Each turbine creates a wake effect that subtracts ten percent of its own effective wind speed from the effective wind speed of the next turbine in line. The power generated by any turbine is equal to the square of its effective wind speed. Maintain a running calculation of the degraded wind speed as you iterate through the sequence, updating the available wind for the next unit. Return a list of power outputs rounded to the nearest integer. For example, given a constant incoming wind of [10, 10, 10], the output is [100, 81, 66].

title: Wi-Fi Signal Strength
spec: Write a function `measure(devices)` that takes a list of lists, where each inner list contains two integers representing the horizontal and vertical coordinates of a connected device relative to a central router. The coverage area consists of concentric zones. A device within a radius of ten units receives a signal strength of ten, within twenty units receives a nine, and so forth, dropping by one unit for every ten distance units. Calculate the Euclidean distance for each device, determine its signal bracket, and sum the total signal strength provided by the router. Devices beyond one hundred units drop the connection and score zero. Keep track of the accumulating total and the individual distances. Return the total integer signal strength. For example, given [[0, 5], [30, 40], [100, 100]], the output is 16.

title: Car Wash Queue Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(cars)` that accepts a list of lists, where each inner list contains an integer arrival time in minutes and an integer wash duration in minutes. The car wash has a single bay that processes one car at a time. If a car arrives when the bay is empty, it enters immediately. If the bay is occupied, the car must wait in a queue. Track the current simulation time, the queue of waiting cars, and the departure time for each vehicle. Progress the clock based on the completion of washes or the arrival of new cars. Return a list of integer departure times in the same order as the input. For example, given [[10, 15], [15, 20], [40, 10]], the output is [25, 45, 50].

title: Pizza Order Assembler
spec: Write a function `assemble(orders)` that takes a list of lists representing incoming pizza requests, where each request has an integer arrival time and an integer baking duration. The kitchen oven can bake up to three pizzas simultaneously. Track the current time, the list of pizzas currently in the oven along with their completion times, and a queue of waiting requests. As time advances, remove finished pizzas to free up oven slots and insert waiting pizzas immediately if space allows. Return a list of completion times for all orders in the sequence they were provided. For example, given [[0, 10], [0, 15], [0, 20], [5, 10]], the first three enter immediately, and the fourth enters at minute ten, resulting in [10, 15, 20, 20].

title: Music Metronome Clicker
spec: Write a function `click(tempos)` that accepts a list of pairs, where each pair contains an integer beats per minute and an integer duration in beats. The function must calculate the exact timestamp in milliseconds for each beat from the beginning of the song. The first beat always occurs at zero milliseconds. Track the elapsed time, convert the current tempo into a millisecond interval per beat, and generate timestamps for the specified duration before moving to the next tempo block. Return a list of integer millisecond timestamps. For example, given [[60, 2], [120, 2]], the output is [0, 1000, 2000, 2500].

title: Aquarium Filter Cycle
spec: Write a function `cycle(days)` that takes an integer number of days to simulate the biological cycle of an aquarium. On each day, fish waste generates two units of ammonia and decaying food generates one additional unit. Beneficial bacteria grow gradually: every day, the ammonia eating bacteria consume an amount of ammonia equal to the current day number, converting it directly into nitrite. Similarly, nitrite eating bacteria consume an amount of nitrite equal to half the current day number rounded down, converting it into nitrate. Finally, aquatic plants absorb one unit of nitrate per day. Track the total accumulated levels of ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate, ensuring none drop below zero at any point. Return a list containing the final levels of ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate. For example, given 3 days, the output is [3, 4, 0].

title: Skipping Rope Contest
spec: Write a function `analyze(jumps)` that accepts a list of integers representing the millisecond timestamps of consecutive jumps in a skipping rope contest. A jump is considered part of a valid streak if the time elapsed since the previous jump is between three hundred and five hundred milliseconds inclusive. If a jump falls outside this window, the current streak resets to one, and the current jump becomes the start of a new potential streak. Iterate over the timestamps, compute the differences between consecutive jumps, and track the current streak length, the maximum streak length achieved, and the starting timestamp of that maximum streak. Return a list containing the maximum integer streak and its starting timestamp. For example, given [0, 400, 800, 1600, 2000, 2400], the output is [3, 1600].

title: Convex Hull Generator
spec: Write a function `graham(points)` that takes a list of coordinate arrays, each containing an x and y number. The function must compute the convex hull of these points using the standard scanning algorithm. First, find the point with the lowest y coordinate, breaking ties with the lowest x coordinate. Sort the remaining points based on the polar angle with the lowest point. Iterate through the sorted points, maintaining a stack of the hull vertices. For each point, while the stack has at least two points and the cross product of the vector from the second to top point to the top point and the vector from the top point to the current point indicates a non left turn, remove the top point from the stack. Push the current point onto the stack. Return the final stack as a list of coordinate arrays. Example input: a list of four corners of a square and one center point. Expected output: the four corner points in counterclockwise order.

title: Elo Rating Updater
spec: Write a function `rate(matches)` that takes a list of arrays. Each array represents a match and contains three elements: a player one string, a player two string, and a result number which is one for a player one win, zero for a player one loss, and half for a draw. The function should track the rating for every player, initializing any unseen player to twelve hundred. Process each match sequentially. For a match, calculate the expected score for player one as one divided by one plus ten raised to the power of the difference of player two rating and player one rating divided by four hundred. Do the symmetric calculation for player two. Multiply the difference between the actual result and expected score by a K factor of thirty two, and add this to the player's rating. Return a list of arrays containing each player string and their final rounded integer rating, sorted alphabetically by player name. Example: two players play one match resulting in a win for player one, outputting player one with twelve hundred sixteen and player two with eleven hundred eighty four.

title: Ray Casting Point Locator
spec: Write a function `count(points, polygons)` that takes a list of point arrays (x and y numbers) and a list of polygons, where each polygon is a list of point arrays. The function must determine how many points lie strictly inside each polygon. For each polygon, iterate through every point. Use the ray casting algorithm by drawing a horizontal line to the right of the point and counting how many polygon edges cross this ray. An edge crosses the ray if one endpoint's y coordinate is strictly greater than the point's y coordinate and the other endpoint's y coordinate is less than or equal to the point's y coordinate, and the x coordinate of the intersection is strictly greater than the point's x coordinate. Return a list of integer counts corresponding to the list of polygons. Example input: a single point at origin, and a square polygon from minus one to one. Expected output: a list containing a count of one.

title: Huffman Tree Builder
spec: Write a function `encode(text)` that takes a plain string and returns a list of binary string encodings for each character in the order they first appear. First, count the frequency of each character in the string. Create a list of leaf nodes containing the character and its frequency. While there is more than one node in the list, sort the list by frequency ascending, remove the two nodes with the lowest frequencies, and create a new parent node whose frequency is their sum. Assign the first removed node as the left child and the second as the right child, then add the parent back to the list. Traverse the final tree to assign a binary zero to left branches and a binary one to right branches, building a binary string for each character. Collect these binary strings into a list. Example input: a string with three as, two bs, and one c. Expected output: a list of three binary strings, such as zero, one zero, and one one.

title: Reverse Polish Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(expressions)` that takes a list of strings, where each string is a mathematical expression in reverse polish notation. The function must evaluate each expression and return a list of numeric results. For each expression, split the string by spaces to get tokens. Iterate through the tokens from left to right. Maintain a stack of numbers. If a token is a number, convert it to a float and push it onto the stack. If the token is an operator (addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division), pop the top two numbers from the stack. Apply the operator using the second popped number as the left operand and the first popped number as the right operand, and push the result back onto the stack. After processing all tokens, the final number on the stack is the result for that expression. Example input: a list with one string containing three, four, and an addition sign. Expected output: a list containing seven.

title: Levenshtein Distance Matrix
spec: Write a function `matrix(words)` that takes a list of strings. The function must calculate the edit distance between every possible pair of words in the list and return a two dimensional list of integers representing this distance matrix. To find the distance between two words, initialize a grid of numbers with rows corresponding to the characters of the first word plus one, and columns for the second word plus one. Fill the first row and column with incrementing numbers representing base deletion and insertion costs. Iterate through each cell of the grid. If the characters match, the cost is the value from the top left diagonal cell. Otherwise, the cost is one plus the minimum of the cell above, the cell to the left, and the cell to the top left. The bottom right cell of the grid holds the final distance for the pair. Example input: a list with two words, kitten and sitting. Expected output: a two by two matrix with zeros on the diagonal and threes off the diagonal.

title: K Means Clusterer
spec: Write a function `cluster(numbers, groups)` that takes a list of floats and an integer indicating the desired number of groups. The function should partition the numbers into the specified number of clusters using a one dimensional k means algorithm. Initialize the centroids by taking the first elements of the sorted input list evenly spaced. Loop to refine the clusters until no numbers change their group assignment. In each iteration, create empty lists for each group. For every number, calculate the absolute difference between it and each centroid, and place the number into the list of the closest centroid. After assigning all numbers, update each centroid to be the average of the numbers in its group. If a group is empty, leave its centroid unchanged. Return a list of the final group lists. Example input: list of one, two, and ten, with two groups. Expected output: a list containing a list of one and two, and a list of ten.

title: Base Sixty Four Encoder
spec: Write a function `encode(bytes)` that takes a list of integers from zero to two hundred fifty five. The function must convert this list into a base sixty four encoded string. Create a lookup string of the uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, plus, and slash. Iterate through the input list three numbers at a time. Combine the three eight bit numbers into a single twenty four bit integer using bitwise operations. Extract four six bit chunks from this integer, and map each chunk to the corresponding character in the lookup string. Append these characters to a result string. If the final group has only one number, pad it with two zero bytes, encode, and replace the last two characters with equal signs. If it has two numbers, pad with one zero byte, encode, and replace the last character with an equal sign. Return the final string. Example input: list of three integers seventy, eighty, and ninety. Expected output: a string of four encoded characters.

title: Comma Separated Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(text)` that takes a single formatted string. The function must parse it into a list of lists of strings, correctly handling fields enclosed in double quotes. Iterate through the characters of the text one by one. Maintain a flag to track whether the current position is inside double quotes, and variables for the current field string and the current row list. If a quote is encountered, toggle the inside quotes flag. If a comma is encountered and the flag is false, add the current field to the row list and clear the field. If a newline is encountered and the flag is false, add the current field to the row, add the row to the main list of rows, and reset both. Otherwise, append the character to the current field. Return the accumulated list of rows. Example input: a string with two values separated by a comma. Expected output: a list containing one list with two string elements.

title: Dijkstra Route Finder
spec: Write a function `navigate(graph, start, end)` that takes a list of network links, a starting point string, and a destination string. Each link is an array containing a source string, a target string, and a numeric distance. The function must find the shortest path from the start to the end. Build an adjacency list mapping each point to its neighbors and distances. Keep a dictionary of shortest known distances from the start, initialized to infinity, and a dictionary of previous points. Set the start distance to zero. Maintain a list of unvisited points. Loop until the unvisited list is empty. Find the unvisited point with the lowest known distance. If it is the destination, stop. For each neighbor of this current point, calculate the distance through the current point. If this new distance is less than the known distance, update the distance and the previous point dictionary. Reconstruct the path by backtracking from the destination to the start and return it as a list of strings. Example input: three connected points. Expected output: the shortest sequence of point strings.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
spec: Write a function `subsequence(strings)` that takes a list containing exactly two strings. The function must compute and return their longest common subsequence as a string. Create a two dimensional grid of numbers with rows equal to the length of the first string plus one, and columns equal to the length of the second string plus one, initialized to zero. Iterate through the characters of both strings. If the characters match, set the grid cell to one plus the value of the diagonal cell to the top left. If they do not match, set the cell to the maximum of the cell above and the cell to the left. Once the grid is filled, start from the bottom right cell and backtrack. If the characters of the strings match at the current indices, prepend the character to a result string and move diagonally top left. Otherwise, move in the direction of the larger grid value. Return the result string. Example input: two strings abc and ac. Expected output: the string ac.

title: Matrix Determinant Calculator
spec: Write a function `determinant(matrix)` that takes a list of lists of floats representing a square grid of numbers. The function must compute and return the mathematical determinant of this grid. If the grid is a single number, return that number. If the grid is two by two, return the product of the top left and bottom right minus the product of the top right and bottom left. For larger grids, use recursive expansion along the first row. Initialize a total sum to zero. Loop through each column of the first row. For each element, create a smaller grid by removing the first row and the current column. Calculate the determinant of this smaller grid recursively. Multiply this sub determinant by the element and by an alternating sign (positive for even columns, negative for odd). Add this product to the total sum. Return the total sum. Example input: a two by two grid with numbers one, two, three, and four. Expected output: minus two.

title: Page Rank Iteration
spec: Write a function `rank(links, iterations)` that takes a list of directed connections between web pages (each connection is an array of source string and target string) and an integer number of steps. The function must compute the rank of each page. First, identify all unique pages and build two structures: one tracking the list of incoming connections for each page, and one tracking the count of outgoing connections for each page. Initialize the rank of each page to one divided by the total number of pages. For each step, calculate a new rank for every page. The new rank is the damping factor of zero point eight five times the sum of the current ranks of all incoming pages divided by their respective outgoing connection counts, plus one minus the damping factor divided by the total pages. Update all ranks simultaneously. Return a list of arrays containing the page string and its final rank float, sorted by rank descending. Example input: two pages where page one links to page two, and one iteration. Expected output: sorted list of the two pages with their computed ranks.

title: Snake Game Updater
spec: Write a function `tick(state, direction)` that takes a current game state and a directional movement array containing an x and y change. The game state is a list containing the grid width, grid height, a list of coordinate arrays for the snake body segments (head first), and a list of coordinate arrays for food items. The function must compute the next frame. Calculate the new head position by adding the direction values to the first segment of the snake body. If the new head falls outside the zero indexed width or height bounds, or if it matches any existing body segment, return an empty list to indicate game over. Check if the new head matches any food coordinates. If it does, create a new food list excluding the eaten item, and do not remove the last segment of the snake body. If no food is eaten, remove the last segment. Add the new head to the beginning of the body. Return the updated state list in the same format. Example input: a snake at five five moving right to six five where food is located. Expected output: snake length increases by one, food removed.

title: Tic Tac Toe Minimax
spec: Write a function `best(board, player)` that takes a list of nine strings representing a three by three grid (each string is either x, o, or empty) and a string indicating the current player (x or o). The function must return the integer index from zero to eight for the optimal next move using the minimax algorithm. First, check if the board has a winning line for either player or is full, returning a high score for a win, a low score for a loss, or zero for a draw. If the game is not over, iterate through all empty indices. For each empty spot, place the current player's mark, recursively call the algorithm for the opponent to evaluate the board, and then remove the mark. Track the maximum score if it is the original player's turn, or the minimum score if it is the opponent's turn. Return the index associated with the best score for the original player. Example input: a board with two xs in a row and one empty spot to win. Expected output: the index of the winning spot.

title: Trie Autocompleter
spec: Write a function `complete(words, prefix)` that takes a list of vocabulary strings and a search string. The function must return a list of all vocabulary words that start with the search string. First, build a prefix tree from the vocabulary list. Create a root node object. For each word, iterate through its characters, creating nested objects for each letter and marking the final node with an end boolean flag.
