The function must return a list of two numbers: the count of ready wheels and the sum of the selling prices of all ready wheels. For a ten kilogram wheel aged eight months with a ten percent target, the final weight is roughly eight point eight kilograms, and its price is one hundred seventy seven dollars.

title: Sundial Shadow Projector
spec: Write `shadow(times)`. The input is a list of hours from solar noon, where positive means afternoon and negative means morning. The sundial gnomon has a height of ten centimeters. For each hour, calculate the sun angle by multiplying the hour by fifteen degrees, then convert to radians. The shadow length is the height divided by the cosine of the sun angle, taking the absolute value. If the hour is before minus four or after four, the shadow is capped at fifty centimeters. Calculate the shadow azimuth angle in degrees, which is the hour multiplied by fifteen, plus one hundred and eighty degrees. Calculate the tip speed, which is the absolute difference in shadow length between the current hour and the previous hour in the list, defaulting to zero for the first hour. Return a list of shadow lengths and azimuth angles rounded to one decimal place. For noon, the shadow is ten and azimuth is one hundred eighty.

title: Incense Burn Time Predictor
spec: Implement `burn(sticks)`. The input is a list of incense sticks with length in centimeters, thickness in millimeters, and a binder ratio. The base burn rate is zero point five centimeters per minute. The adjusted burn rate is the base rate divided by the thickness, and further reduced by the binder ratio multiplied by zero point two. Calculate the total burn time by dividing the length by the adjusted burn rate. If the thickness is greater than three millimeters, add ten minutes to account for the slow smoldering core. Calculate the smoke volume produced, which is the length times the square of the thickness times three point one four. Return a list of total burn times in minutes and smoke volumes, rounded to the nearest integer. For a twenty centimeter stick, two millimeters thick, and a zero point one binder ratio, the burn rate is zero point two four, yielding eighty three minutes and two hundred fifty one smoke volume.

title: Glassblowing Annealing Schedule
spec: Write `anneal(pieces)`. The input is a list of glass pieces with thickness in inches and a color tint integer. The annealing process requires soaking at a high temperature, then slowly cooling. The soak time in hours is the thickness squared multiplied by two. The cooling rate is twenty degrees per hour divided by the thickness. The total time spent cooling from nine hundred degrees to four hundred degrees is five hundred divided by the cooling rate. If the color tint is greater than five, the glass is opaque and requires an extra hour of soak time. Calculate the energy cost of the cycle, which is the soak time multiplied by fifteen kilowatts plus the cooling time multiplied by five kilowatts. Return a list containing the total annealing time, which is soak time plus cooling time, and the energy cost for each piece, rounded to one decimal place. For a one inch piece with tint three, soak is two, cooling is twenty five, time is twenty seven, and energy is one hundred fifty five.

title: Parade Float Weight Balancer
spec: Create `balance(floats)`. The input is a list of parade floats where each has a length in meters and a list of elements. Each element has a weight in kilograms and a position in meters from the front of the float. Calculate the total weight of each float by summing the weights of all elements. Then, calculate the center of gravity by summing the product of each element weight and its position, and dividing by the total weight. Calculate the turning radius, which is the float length squared divided by the distance between the front and the center of gravity. If the center of gravity is not within twenty percent of the middle of the float, or if the total weight exceeds five thousand kilograms, the float is unsafe. Return a list of boolean values representing the safety of each float, and their calculated turning radii. For a ten meter float with a thousand kilogram element at two meters and a thousand at eight meters, the center is at five meters, it is safe, and the turning radius is twenty.

title: Bocce Ball Scorer
spec: Implement `score(rounds)`. The input is a list of game rounds. Each round has the coordinates of the small target ball, a list of coordinates for the red team balls, and a list of coordinates for the blue team balls. All coordinates are lists of two numbers. Compute the distance of the target ball from the starting line at zero zero. If the target ball is less than five units away, the round is invalid and yields zero points. Otherwise, compute the distance from each team ball to the target ball using the Pythagorean theorem. Find the minimum distance for both teams. The team with the smaller minimum distance wins the round. The winning team scores one point for every ball that is closer to the target than the closest ball of the opposing team. Return a list with the total red score and total blue score across all rounds. For a round where red has balls at distance two and four, and blue at distance three, red scores one point.

title: Cider Fermentation Tracker
spec: Write `ferment(vats)`. The input is a list of cider batches containing initial gravity, current gravity, and temperature. Calculate the alcohol by volume for each batch by subtracting the current gravity from the initial gravity and multiplying by one hundred thirty one point two five. Find the fermentation speed by taking the gravity difference and dividing it by the temperature minus ten. If the alcohol by volume exceeds eight percent, the yeast becomes stressed and the speed is halved. Calculate the residual sugar as the current gravity minus one, multiplied by a thousand. Calculate the carbonation level, which is the residual sugar multiplied by zero point five, capped at a maximum of three volumes. Return a list containing the alcohol by volume and the carbonation level rounded to two decimal places for each batch. For an initial gravity of one point zero five and current of one point zero one at twenty degrees, the alcohol is five point two five and carbonation is five capped to three.

title: Gargoyle Water Flow Model
spec: Create `flow(buildings)`. The input is a list of structures, each with a roof area in square meters, a rainfall intensity in millimeters per hour, and a count of gargoyle spouts. The total water collected per minute is the roof area times the rainfall intensity divided by sixty. The capacity of a single gargoyle is fifteen liters per minute. Calculate the total capacity by multiplying the count by fifteen. If the collected water exceeds the total capacity, the roof floods and the excess water is the difference between collected and capacity. The function must calculate the volume of water expelled by each spout, which is the collected water divided by the count, capped at fifteen. Calculate the kinetic energy of the expelled water falling ten meters, which is the expelled volume times nine point eight times ten. Return a list of the excess water volumes and the spout kinetic energies for each building. For a roof of one hundred area and rainfall of sixty with five spouts, collected is one hundred, capacity is seventy five, excess is twenty five, and expelled is fifteen.

title: Bonsai Pruning Scheduler
spec: Write `prune(trees)`. The input is a list of bonsai trees, each specifying a species name, current leaf count, growth rate per week, and a maximum allowed leaf count. For each tree, calculate how many weeks it will take for the current leaf count to exceed the maximum allowed leaf count. This is found by subtracting the current count from the maximum, and dividing by the growth rate. If the species is a juniper, the growth rate is reduced by ten percent before the calculation due to slow winter growth. Calculate the fertilizer needed per week, which is the current leaf count multiplied by zero point zero one grams. Find the tree that requires pruning the soonest. Return a list containing the name of the tree to prune first, the number of weeks until it needs pruning rounded up, and its weekly fertilizer requirement. For a pine with fifty leaves, growing ten per week, with a max of ninety, it takes four weeks and needs zero point five grams of fertilizer.

title: Surfboard Buoyancy Calculator
spec: Implement `float(boards)`. The input is a list of boards with length in centimeters, average width in centimeters, average thickness in centimeters, and foam density. Calculate the volume of each board by multiplying length, width, and thickness, then converting to liters by dividing by one thousand. The buoyant force is the volume in liters. The total weight the board must support is the rider weight, fixed at eighty kilograms, plus the board weight, which is the volume multiplied by the foam density. Calculate the drag coefficient, which is the width divided by the length, plus the thickness multiplied by zero point one. If the buoyant force is greater than the total weight plus ten, the board floats perfectly. Return a list of the calculated volumes in liters and drag coefficients for boards that float perfectly. For a board of two hundred length, fifty width, and five thickness, the volume is fifty liters and drag coefficient is zero point seven five.

title: Rock Climbing Route Grader
spec: Create `grade(routes)`. The input is a list of climbing routes containing total height in meters, average overhang angle in degrees, and a list of hold sizes. Each hold size is a number from one to ten, where one is smallest. Calculate a base difficulty by dividing the height by the average hold size. Add an angle penalty of two points for every degree of overhang above ten. If the route has fewer than twenty holds, multiply the total difficulty by one point five to account for long reaches. Calculate the estimated climb time in minutes, which is the height multiplied by two, plus five minutes for every overhanging degree. The final grade score is an integer mapped directly from the difficulty calculation. Return a list of lists, where each inner list contains the integer difficulty score and the estimated climb time for each route. For a twenty meter route with average hold size two and no overhang, the score is ten and time is forty minutes.

title: Blacksmith Forging Time
spec: Write `forge(metals)`. The input is a list of forging jobs, each containing a starting thickness in millimeters, a target thickness, and a carbon content percentage. In each heating cycle, the blacksmith can reduce the thickness by five millimeters. Calculate the number of cycles required by finding the difference between starting and target thickness, dividing by five, and rounding up. The time for each cycle is ten minutes of heating plus five minutes of hammering. If the carbon content is above zero point eight, the metal is harder and the hammering time per cycle doubles. Calculate the total forging time for each job by multiplying the number of cycles by the time per cycle. Calculate the fuel consumed, which is two kilograms of coal per heating cycle, plus an extra kilogram if the hammering time was doubled. Return a list of total times in minutes and total fuel consumed. For a twenty millimeter bar reduced to ten with zero point five carbon, two cycles take thirty minutes and consume four kilograms of coal.

title: Vinyl Record Groove Spacing
spec: Implement `groove(records)`. The input is a list of records with a rotation speed in revolutions per minute, an outer radius in millimeters, an inner radius in millimeters, and a track pitch in millimeters per revolution. The usable radial space is the outer radius minus the inner radius. The total number of revolutions the record can hold is the usable radial space divided by the track pitch. Calculate the total playback time in minutes by dividing the total revolutions by the rotation speed. If the track pitch is less than zero point zero five, subtract two minutes from the playback time due to the wider grooves needed for bass frequencies. Calculate the linear velocity at the outer radius in millimeters per second, which is the rotation speed times the outer radius times two times three point one four, divided by sixty. Return a list of playback times in minutes and linear velocities, rounded to two decimal places, for each record. For a thirty three speed record, outer radius one hundred forty, inner radius sixty, pitch zero point one, time is twenty four point two four and velocity is four hundred eighty three point five six.
